# Lamentations 1 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** How deserted the city sits — once so full of people! She was great among the nations, like a queen — but now she's like a widow. Once a princess, now a slave.

**2** She cries through the night, tears streaming down her face. Of all her lovers, not one is there to comfort her. All her friends have betrayed her — they've become her enemies.

**3** Judah has been dragged into exile — driven out by oppression and harsh slavery. She lives among the nations now but finds no place to rest. Her enemies caught up with her when she had nowhere to turn.

**4** The roads to Zion weep — no one comes to the festivals anymore. Her gates are deserted. Her priests moan. Her young women grieve. And Zion herself — she is drowning in bitterness.

**5** Her enemies are on top now; her foes are comfortable and prosperous. Why? Because the LORD Himself has punished her for her many sins. Her children have been taken away as prisoners.

**6** All the beauty and majesty have drained from Jerusalem. Her leaders are like starving deer searching desperately for pasture — stumbling along with no strength left, chased by their hunters.

**7** In her days of suffering and homelessness, Jerusalem looks back and remembers all the wonderful things she once had. When she fell to the enemy and no one came to help, her enemies just watched and laughed at her destruction.

**8** Jerusalem's sin was enormous — and now she's treated like trash. Everyone who once admired her now despises her, because they've seen her shame. She groans and hides her face.

**9** Her filth clung to her clothes, but she never thought about where she was headed. Her downfall was staggering — and no one was there to comfort her. "LORD, look at how I'm suffering! The enemy has won!"

**10** The enemy has grabbed everything precious she had. She watched helplessly as foreign nations marched into her holy Temple — nations You specifically told her were never allowed in.

**11** All her people groan as they search for food. They trade their most treasured possessions for a scrap of bread just to stay alive. "Look at me, LORD, and see how worthless I've become."

**12** "Does no one care? All you people passing by — look at me! Is there any suffering like mine? The LORD did this to me on the day of His furious anger.

**13** He sent fire from heaven that burned deep into my bones. He set a trap for my feet and sent me sprawling. He left me stunned and sick, all day long.

**14** He wove my sins into a yoke and tied it around my neck with His own hands. It crushed my strength. The Lord handed me over to people I could never fight off.

**15** The Lord swept aside every warrior I had. He called an army against me to destroy my young men. The Lord has trampled the young women of Judah like grapes in a winepress.

**16** This is why I weep — my eyes overflow with tears. No one is here to comfort me or restore my strength. My children are left with nothing, because the enemy has won."

**17** Jerusalem reaches out her hands, but no one takes them. The LORD has turned Jacob's neighbors into his enemies. Jerusalem has become disgusting to everyone around her.

**18** "The LORD is right to do this — I rebelled against Him. But listen, all you nations, and look at my pain! My young men and women have been carried into captivity.

**19** I begged my allies for help, but they let me down. My priests and elders starved to death in the city while desperately searching for food.

**20** LORD, see my agony! My insides are churning. My heart is breaking — because I was so rebellious. Outside, the sword kills. Inside, there is nothing but death.

**21** People hear me crying, but no one comforts me. All my enemies are thrilled about what You've done to me. Bring the day of judgment You promised — let them suffer as I have!

**22** Let all their wickedness come before You! Punish them as You've punished me for all my sins. I can't stop groaning, and my heart is ready to give out."

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **1:1**: The contrast is devastating — 'great among nations' to 'like a widow.' Lamentations doesn't explain the suffering away. It sits in it. That's its gift.

- **1:12**: This is one of the rawest lines in Scripture — 'Is there any pain like mine?' Jerusalem isn't asking for theology. She's asking if anyone even notices.

- **1:16**: The repeated 'my eye, my eye' captures the physical reality of grief that won't stop. Lamentations gives permission to weep without apology.

— PNEUMA
